postcard.kicker: Marcus · notes for a victory celebration
body: The war ends, and Secretary Seward calls it her victory. At home in Auburn, her parents ask where her pay is.
Build the house on South Street, stocked and ready for peace.
postcard.word: A furlough is leave from the army. Harriet finally takes one.

mission.h: Stock the house on South Street
mission.p: Fill the woodshed and shelves, set the rockers on the porch, lay out her papers.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. the house, two rocking chairs on the porch
  2. the woodshed: a pile of firewood
  3. the shelves: a flour sack and the jars of jelly
  4. on a chair: her pocketful of papers

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows the house, rockers, firewood and shelves, and you say 2 sentences: one thing at the house, what it shows Harriet won, and what she was still owed, with a detail from Chapter 19.

alt.p: Chapter 19 moves between four places. Put each moment where it happened.
alt.gameH: Tap a moment, then tap its place

items.t: neighbors bring more calf’s-foot jelly than anyone could eat
items.why: Auburn’s leading citizens flock to the little house when word spreads that Hat is sick.

items.t: seven dollars a month against thirteen
items.why: Old Rit asks where the pay is. Harriet explains the colored troops refused the unequal seven dollars.
She hears it sitting in Secretary Seward’s office while he sorts her papers.

items.t: Seward says it is her victory
items.why: She fought for it long before the rest of us did, he tells her.

items.t: an army armed with scrub brushes and mops
items.why: In a few days she organizes freedmen and women to clean the filthy hospital.

items.t: she is made Matron of the Hospital
items.why: The Surgeon General tells her so in Washington, in the mourning city.

items.t: a pass that says Hospital nurse, half fare
items.why: The conductor does not care what the paper says. It takes three men to force her into the baggage car.

alt.miss: Not there. Think about where Harriet was standing when it happened.

write.q: Pick one thing at the house on South Street: the porch rockers, the woodshed, the shelves, the jars of jelly or the papers. In 2 sentences, say what it shows Harriet won and what she was still owed, with one detail from Chapter 19.
starters: But she was still owed ___ because ___.

scripts.brief: Hey, it’s Marcus. In Chapter 19 the war ends. Secretary Seward tells Harriet it is her victory. But at home in Auburn, Old Rit wants to know where her pay is, and the woodshed and the kitchen shelves are empty. Build the little house on South Street the way Harriet meant to leave it: stocked, warm, and ready for a life of peace. Then tell me what she won, and what she was still owed.
scripts.alt: No headset? Sit on the porch with me. Chapter 19 moves between Auburn, Washington, the hospital at Fortress Monroe, and a train. Put each moment where it happened, and you will see how far Harriet traveled in one chapter.
scripts.saved: The house is stocked and the rockers are on the porch. Here is your quilt square. Keep it, and remember that the people Harriet fought for still owed her something.

testPara: The jars of jelly show Harriet won friends and neighbors in Auburn. But she was still owed her pay because the government never sent the eighteen hundred dollars.
